units: <cite ref="Aramaic Targum to Job 24:3">Targ. Job XXIV, 3</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 68a:9">B. Mets. 68ᵃ</cite> <he>מ׳ ליה פלניא וכ׳</he> (not <cite ref="M02900"><he>משכון</he></cite>) A pledged his field to B, and then rented it from him.
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 73b:1">Ib. 73ᵇ</cite> top <he>ר׳ מרי … מ׳ ליה וכ׳</he> a gentile gave his house (for occupation) as a pledge, and then sold it to &c.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 113a:7">Ib. 113ᵃ</cite> <he>אבל מַשְׁכּוּנֵי לא</he> Ms. M. (ed. <he>מַשְׁכְּנוֹ</he>) but to take a pledge out of his house he (the messenger of the court) is not permitted; a. fr.—Part. pass. <cite ref="M02904"><he>מְמַשְׁכַּן</he></cite>, f. <cite ref="M02908"><he>מְמַשְׁכְּנָא</he></cite>.
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 3:2">Koh. R. to III, 2</cite>, v. <cite ref="M00804"><he>מְחַבַּלְתָּא</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 73b:1">B. Mets. 73ᵇ</cite> <he>אי הוה ידענא דממשכן וכ׳</he> Ms. F. (Ms. M. <he>דמשכן</he>, corr. acc.; ed. <he>דהוה ממוּשְׁכָּן</he>) if I had known that the house was pledged to you. Y. ib. VIII, end, 11ᵈ <he>ביתיה הוות מְמַשְׁכְּנָה וכ׳</he> his house was pledged to &c.; a. e.

senses.gloss: to be given as a pledge; to be levied upon; to borrow on pledge.
